questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Tiger, Leopard, Crocodile, Cheetah

options.option_text: Tiger (tiger is a wild cat — same category as others)
Leopard (leopard is a wild cat — same category)
Crocodile (correct: Tiger, Leopard, Cheetah are all wild cats (felines); Crocodile is a reptile — the odd one out ✓)
Cheetah (cheetah is the fastest wild cat — but still a feline, not the odd one)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Tiger, Leopard, and Cheetah are all members of the family Felidae (wild cats). Crocodile is a reptile. It does not belong to the cat family.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Violin, Guitar, Sitar, Flute, Tabla

options.option_text: Guitar (string instrument — like violin and sitar)
Flute (correct: Violin, Guitar, Sitar, Tabla are played with hands by plucking/hitting/bowing; Flute is a wind instrument — the only one in this group ✓)
Tabla (Tabla is a percussion instrument — but the question groups all types; focus: Flute is the only wind/breath instrument)
Sitar (string instrument — same category as guitar and violin)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Violin, Guitar, and Sitar are string instruments. Tabla is a percussion instrument. Flute is a wind instrument — the only one played by blowing air into it. In the classification of string vs wind vs percussion, Flute stands apart as the only wind instrument in this group.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: CUP : SAUCER :: PENCIL : ERASER :: BREAD : BUTTER :: LOCK : ?

options.option_text: Door (lock and door are both parts of an entry — not a pair like the others)
Key (correct: CUP:SAUCER, PENCIL:ERASER, BREAD:BUTTER are all complementary pairs used together; LOCK:KEY is the same type of pair ✓)
Chain (lock and chain are sometimes used together but KEY is the direct functional complement)
Handle (lock and handle are on the same object but not a complementary-use pair like the others)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The pattern is complementary pairs: Cup-Saucer (used together), Pencil-Eraser (used together), Bread-Butter (used together). Lock-Key completes the pattern — the key is the functional complement of the lock, just as the eraser is the functional complement of the pencil.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Gonorrhoea, Malaria, Tuberculosis, Cholera, Typhoid

options.option_text: Gonorrhoea (sexually transmitted bacterial disease — not vector-borne or food/water-borne)
Malaria (correct: Gonorrhoea, Tuberculosis, Cholera, Typhoid are caused by bacteria; Malaria is caused by a protozoan (Plasmodium) — the odd one out ✓)
Tuberculosis (caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis — bacterial)
Cholera (caused by Vibrio cholerae — bacterial)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Gonorrhoea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), Cholera (Vibrio cholerae), and Typhoid (Salmonella typhi) are all BACTERIAL diseases. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium (a protozoan parasite), transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito. Malaria is the odd one out.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: BIDE, HIDE, SIDE, TIDE, WIDE, FIDE

options.option_text: BIDE (real English word: to bide time = to wait)
HIDE (real word: to conceal)
FIDE (correct: BIDE, HIDE, SIDE, TIDE, WIDE are all valid English words; FIDE is a Latin word meaning 'faith' — not a standard standalone English word ✓)
TIDE (real word: the rise and fall of sea levels)

questions.explanation: C is correct. BIDE, HIDE, SIDE, TIDE, WIDE are all standard English words (verbs/nouns). FIDE is Latin (used in phrases like 'bona fide' = in good faith), not a standalone English word. It is the odd one out in a list of English dictionary words.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Rupee, Dollar, Pound, Franc, Yen, Peso, Drachma, Euro

options.option_text: Euro (Euro is the official currency of the Eurozone — still active)
Drachma (correct: Rupee, Dollar, Pound, Franc (Switzerland), Yen, Peso, Euro are all CURRENT currencies; Drachma was the currency of Greece, replaced by Euro in 2002 — the only defunct currency ✓)
Peso (still in use in multiple Latin American countries)
Franc (Swiss Franc is still in use)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Drachma was the currency of Greece and was discontinued in 2002 when Greece adopted the Euro. All others (Rupee=India, Dollar=USA/others, Pound=UK, Franc=Switzerland, Yen=Japan, Peso=Mexico and others, Euro=Eurozone) are currently in active use. Drachma is the only historical/defunct currency in this list.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Moon, Neptune

options.option_text: Mars (a planet orbiting the Sun)
Jupiter (a planet orbiting the Sun)
Moon (correct: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune are all PLANETS in our solar system; Moon is Earth's natural satellite, not a planet ✓)
Neptune (a planet in our solar system)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and Neptune are all planets in our solar system. The Moon is Earth's natural satellite — it orbits Earth, not the Sun directly. The Moon is the odd one out in a list of planets.
